title: Cancel superseded content searches, and keep index locks off the UI thread
problem: Each run_search replaces `self.search_task` (src/finder/mod.rs:1390), which only drops the foreground future; the grep itself runs synchronously inside `background_spawn` (1397-1399; `content_search` -> `engine.grep`, 2993-3006), so dropping the task cannot stop it. The debounce is the same 50 ms as for name search (1391-1395) and typing is slower than that, so typing `invoice` in Contents mode launches about seven greps, each of which runs to the end: until the page fills, or for rare text until time_limit_secs (5 s by default, crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:378; unbounded with 'None', src/finder/dialogs.rs:171). All greps share fff's one SEARCH_THREAD_POOL (fff-search file_picker.rs:1402), so the query the user is waiting for gets a fraction of the pool, reaches fewer files before its own time limit, and answers seconds late. Clearing the field (set_query, mod.rs:1330-1338) leaves them running too. fff has the hook: GrepSearchOptions::abort_signal (fff-search-0.11.0/src/grep/types.rs:135-139, honoured in file_picker.rs:1397-1400 and checked every 8 files in grep.rs:612-615), but engine.rs:906-932 builds the options with `..Default::default()` and never sets it. Each grep also holds the picker's read lock for its whole run (engine.rs:890-959); the lock is a parking_lot RwLock (fff-search shared.rs:79), where a waiting writer (watcher batch, track_open at engine.rs:1303, git refresh) blocks new readers, including name searches. The index-status poll calls engine.status() on the UI thread every 400 ms while scanning or finishing (mod.rs:1495, 1504; status() takes each picker's read lock and counts every folder, engine.rs:109-126), so the window can stall behind a long grep. The code's own comment at mod.rs:1436-1439 says lock-taking belongs off the UI thread. Engine::search and grep also call the heavy `r.status().scanning` per query (engine.rs:520, 866) though the cheap `scanning()` exists for that (99-107).
proposal: Engine: add `pub fn grep_cancellable(&self, req: &GrepRequest, abort: Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>) -> GrepResponse` (grep() delegates with None, keeping GrepRequest's PartialEq derive); pass `abort_signal: abort.clone()` in GrepSearchOptions, check the flag at the top of the per-root loop (889) and break, and never report `stopped` for an aborted run. Finder: hold `search_abort: AbortOnDrop(Arc<AtomicBool>)` (a newtype whose Drop stores true); `run_search` (1364) and the empty-query branch of `set_query` (1330-1338) replace it, which aborts the previous grep; `content_search` (2993) takes the flag and passes it through. Status: in `poll_index_status` fetch `engine.status()` inside `cx.background_spawn` and assign it in `this.update`, for both the first read (1495) and the loop (1504). In engine.rs lines 520 and 866 use `r.scanning()`. Optional: a longer debounce for contents, `Duration::from_millis(if contents { 250 } else { 50 })` at 1391-1395, noted in src/finder/dialogs.rs (about 1003) and docs/manual.md:324.
original_test_plan: Engine unit test next to `search_settings_change_content_search` (engine.rs:2253): 400 to 1,000 small files each containing `needle`, `wait_ready`; `grep_cancellable` with a flag already set to true returns far fewer hits than files (fff always searches file 0, then stops within the first chunk) and `stopped == false`; with a false flag it returns them all up to the limit. Unit test for AbortOnDrop: dropping or replacing it sets the shared flag. Headless UI test: click `by-contents`, call `set_query("a", true)` then `set_query("atlas", true)` without settling in between, settle, and assert `ui.names() == ["Project Atlas.txt"]` and that the first search's flag (exposed through a `#[doc(hidden)]` accessor like rows_for_test) is set. Existing index-status assertions (indexed_files() > 0 after settle, sidebar footer text) cover the background status poll.
original_risks: A provided `abort_signal` replaces the picker's own cancel flag (file_picker.rs:1397-1400), so a grep on an index that is being torn down runs until the time limit instead of stopping early. The status poll becomes asynchronous, so index_status lags by one hop; tests that read it right after set_search_roots must settle first. An aborted grep returns partial hits that must be discarded (the existing search_gen check already does this). A 250 ms debounce makes contents results feel slightly later on small folders; Return already skips the debounce.

verifier.claim_check:
Every cited fact holds on the real code path; I found no handler elsewhere that cancels a grep.

**Superseded greps run to the end**
- `src/finder/mod.rs:1390` replaces `self.search_task`. Dropping a Task only cancels at an await point (gpui-pre-scheduler `executor.rs:399`, async-task), and the grep is one synchronous call inside `background_spawn` (`mod.rs:1396-1399` -> `content_search` 2993-3006 -> `engine.grep`).
- `search_task` is replaced in only two places: `mod.rs:1332` (query cleared) and `mod.rs:1390`. Neither signals the running grep. The `search_gen` check at 1423 only discards the result.
- The debounce is a flat 50 ms (`mod.rs:1391-1395`), and `InputEvent::Change` calls `set_query(value, false)` (`mod.rs:1304-1306`), so normal typing starts one grep per keystroke.
- The time limit defaults to 5 s (`crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:378`), and 0 / "None" is offered (`src/finder/dialogs.rs:171-176`).
- `content_index` defaults to false (`config.rs:374`), so by default there is no bigram prefilter and a rare-text grep reads files until the limit. This makes the problem worse than the candidate states.
- The limit is applied per root (`engine.rs:924`, inside the loop at 889), so a superseded grep can run N roots x 5 s.

**fff has the hook and the engine does not use it**
- `GrepSearchOptions::abort_signal` is at `fff-search-0.11.0/src/grep/types.rs:135-139`. It is honoured in `file_picker.rs:1397-1400` and 1428-1431, checked every 8th file in `grep/grep.rs:612-615`, and also in `fuzzy_grep.rs:161` and `multi_pattern.rs`. It suppresses the literal-fallback retry at `grep.rs:223`.
- `engine.rs:906-932` ends with `..Default::default()` and never sets it.
- All greps share `SEARCH_THREAD_POOL.install` (`file_picker.rs:1402`, 1433; `parallelism.rs:62`).

**Locks**
- The picker read guard is taken at `engine.rs:890` and lives through 992, because the result borrows the picker.
- The lock is a `parking_lot::RwLock` (`fff-search shared.rs:79`, 120-126), whose `read()` blocks behind a waiting writer.
- Writers exist in normal use: watcher batches (`watcher/background_watcher.rs:558`, 712, 757, 844), scan commits (`scan.rs:186`, 260, 327), and `track_open` (`engine.rs:1303`).
- Consequence: once a writer queues behind old greps, the new grep, name searches (`engine.rs:613`) and `status()` all wait for the old greps to finish.

**Status poll on the UI thread**
- `mod.rs:1495` and `mod.rs:1504` call `engine.status()` on the UI thread. That reaches `engine.rs:400-406` and `RootIndex::status` at 109-126, which takes the read lock and counts all dirs at line 124.
- These are the only picker-lock calls left on the UI thread; search, set_roots, rescan, track_open, folder_stats and roots_indexing are all in `background_spawn`.
- The comment at `mod.rs:1436-1439` states the policy, and CHANGELOG 0.5.1 fixed the same class of stall for folder checks.

**Per-query status call**
- `engine.rs:520` and `engine.rs:866` call `r.status().scanning`. The cheap `scanning()` (99-107) has identical semantics, including the picker-None case.

**Docs and tests**
- Nothing in `docs/manual.md` or `CHANGELOG.md` describes this as intentional. The only pinned text is "50 ms" at `manual.md:324` and `dialogs.rs:1003`.
- No test pins the current behaviour. The only contents-mode test is `tests/controls.rs:371-376`, which toggles the mode and asserts no results.

**Errors in the candidate**
- The test plan says existing assertions cover the status poll (`indexed_files() > 0`, footer text). No test asserts either; grep of `tests/` finds only `ui.exists("index-status")` at `tests/folder_tree.rs:533`.
- The stated risk that an external abort flag stops a torn-down index from cancelling its grep is moot. The picker's `cancelled` flag is only set by `FilePicker::drop`/`cancel` (`file_picker.rs:1900`, 1982) and `Engine::drop` (`engine.rs:1326`), and a running grep holds both the read guard and an `Arc<Engine>`, so neither can happen mid-grep.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Do the core proposal and drop the optional 250 ms debounce.

**1. Engine (`crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs`)**
- Add `pub fn grep_cancellable(&self, req: &GrepRequest, abort: Option<&Arc<AtomicBool>>) -> GrepResponse` and make `grep()` delegate with `None`. This keeps the `PartialEq`/`Default` derives on `GrepRequest` (line 206) and leaves `src/server/mod.rs:477` and the tests at 2137 and 2272 untouched.
- Pass `abort` through the root-spelling recursion at 855-860.
- Set `abort_signal: abort.cloned()` in the options at 906-932.
- Put the abort check after each root's results are merged (next to the limit break at 993), not at the top of the loop. A pre-set flag then goes through fff's own abort path, which searches at most 8 files, so the unit test proves the option is wired. A top-of-loop check would return 0 hits and prove nothing.
- Gate line 962 with `&& !aborted`.
- Lines 520 and 866: use `r.scanning()`.

**2. Finder (`src/finder/mod.rs`)**
- Add `struct AbortOnDrop(Arc<AtomicBool>)` with `Default`, `fn flag(&self) -> Arc<AtomicBool>`, and a `Drop` that stores true.
- Add the field `search_abort` next to `search_task` (304, initialised at 554).
- Replace it in `run_search` beside the `search_gen` bump (1364) and in the empty-query branch of `set_query` (1331-1332). These are the only two places `search_task` is replaced; closing a tab drops the field, which also aborts.
- `content_search` (2993) takes `&Arc<AtomicBool>` and calls `grep_cancellable`.
- Add `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn search_abort_for_test(&self) -> Arc<AtomicBool>` beside `rows_for_test` (683).

**3. Status poll (`mod.rs:1494-1528`)**
- Clone the engine and fetch `engine.status()` in `cx.background_spawn`, both before the loop and after each 400 ms timer.
- Keep the semantics exact: the first fetch only assigns and calls `cx.notify()`. The `was_scanning && !scanning` branch (`detect_terminals`, `run_search`, Recents reload, `reload_folder_stats`) must stay in loop iterations only. Otherwise calling `poll_index_status` again from 1564, 1595 or 1619 could fire an extra `run_search`.
- `index_status` is empty for one hop at window creation, so the footer briefly reads "0 files indexed". Nothing in `Finder::new` after line 662 reads it.

**4. Debounce**
- Leave it at 50 ms. With cancellation a superseded grep stops within about 8 files per worker, so 250 ms only adds latency and would change documented text at `docs/manual.md:324` and `src/finder/dialogs.rs:1003`. No edits to `dialogs.rs` or `manual.md` are needed.

**5. Changelog**
- Add a "Fixed" entry under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Pitfalls**
- Do not put the `Arc<AtomicBool>` in `GrepRequest`; it breaks the derives.
- Abort granularity equals the existing time-limit granularity (same check at `grep.rs:612-615`), so a file being read finishes first.
verifier.test_plan:
All three tests run on Linux with no platform code.

**1. Engine unit test**
- Location: the `mod tests` in `crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs`, next to `search_settings_change_content_search` (about line 2253), using the same pattern: temp dir, `Engine::new(EngineOptions { watch: false, search: Default::default(), .. })`, `engine.wait_ready(..)`.
- Write 400 small files each containing `needle`.
- `grep(&GrepRequest { patterns: vec!["needle".into()], limit: 1000, ..Default::default() })` returns 400 hits.
- `grep_cancellable(&req, Some(&flag))` with the flag pre-set to true returns a non-empty result with fewer than 50 hits, `files_searched < 50`, and `!stopped`. fff always searches file 0 and drops everything from the first skipped index, so the real count is at most 8 on any core count.
- With a false flag it returns 400.
- The `!stopped` assertion is vacuous in a fast test; keep it only as a guard.

**2. `AbortOnDrop` unit test**
- Location: the `mod tests` in `src/finder/mod.rs` (about line 3433). It uses explicit imports, not `super::*`.
- Dropping it, or replacing it through assignment, sets the shared flag.

**3. Headless UI test**
- Location: `tests/controls.rs`, next to `scope_bar_controls` (line 360), using `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.click("by-contents")`, `ui.update`, `ui.names()`, `ui.read`.
- `ui.update` settles after every call (`tests/common/mod.rs:272-280`), so both queries must go in one closure:
  `let first = ui.update(|f, _, cx| { f.set_query("a".into(), true, cx); let first = f.search_abort_for_test(); f.set_query("atlas".into(), true, cx); first });`
- Assert `first.load(..)` is true, the current flag is false, and `ui.names() == ["Project Atlas.txt"]`. The fixture file's content is "atlas" (`tests/common/mod.rs:45`).
- Then clear with `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query(String::new(), true, cx))` and assert the flag captured before clearing is set.
- This test covers the flag plumbing only; the engine test covers the abort itself.

**4. Status poll**
- No existing assertion covers it, so add one to the UI test above: after `Ui::open`, `ui.read(|f| f.indexed_files()) > 0`. `Ui::open_with` ends with `settle()`, which runs the background hop.

I did not run cargo, so none of these assertions have been executed.
verifier.risks:
- **Scope:** the change is small and additive. `grep()` keeps its signature and behaviour for the server and existing tests.
- **Status poll:** `index_status` is empty until the first background hop, so the footer shows "0 files indexed" for a frame at window creation. If the first fetch is run through the scanning-to-idle branch, it can fire an extra `run_search` or `detect_terminals` when `poll_index_status` is called again; keep it assign-only.
- **Abort promptness:** fff checks the flag every 8th file per rayon split, so a superseded grep still finishes the files it is reading (up to `max_file_size`, 10 MB by default) before it releases the read lock. This is the same promptness as the existing time limit.
- **Picker cancel flag:** an external `abort_signal` replaces the picker's own flag, but nothing in this app can set that flag during a grep, so there is no regression.
- **Debounce:** the optional 250 ms change would alter documented behaviour (`manual.md:324`, `dialogs.rs:1003`) for little gain once cancellation exists; leave it out.
- **Unverified:** I could not run cargo. The UI test's `["Project Atlas.txt"]` expectation rests on reading the fixture and the engine grep tests, not on a run.
